newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila grain buyers out of market on ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Manila grain buyers out of market on ample supply.

text.p: Philippine wheat and corn importers are expected to stay away from the market in the coming week due to ample supplies, traders said on Friday.

"Argentina is offering hard wheat for January delivery. But there are no takers yet as local flour millers are closely examining prices," said the chief trader in one of the Philippines' largest flour millers.
The Philippines buys most of its wheat from the United States. It is the 11th largest buyer of wheat in the world, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has said.
The Philippines is being sidelined ahead of the release by the USDA next Tuesday of its November crop report, which is being keenly watched by traders and buyers around the region.
Local traders said suppliers from Argentina, Australia and Canadia are aggressively courting Philippine flour millers.
"Their offers are good -very competitive to U.S. wheat prices. But local buyers are adamant to buy wheat substitutes because traditional Filipino bakers are very selective," said one Manila trader.
The Filipinos are looking for a price below that offered in Minneapolis, where the country buys most of its wheat.
The MGE December futures contract closed on Thursday 3-3/4 U.S. cents up at $3.85-1/4 a bushel.
One trader said Manila-based flour millers were negotiating with the Argentinians to get a discount on that price.
The prevailing retail prices of flour in Manila remained unchanged at 290 pesos per 25 kg for hard flour and 260 pesos for soft flour, the Trade and Industry Department said.

The corn market is also expected to be quiet next week as local feed millers and livestock farmers await the arrival of 150,000 tonnes of yellow corn no 2 they bought at an average price of US$161.10 a tonne C&F last week from the United States.
"I don't expect any more importations for the rest of the year. The next action may come in February 1997," said a trader in a Japanese commodity house.
Traders said they expect the Philippines to import 250,000 tonnes of corn in the first quarter next year to meet rising demand of the commodity.
The private sector usually asks the state-controlled National Food Authority (NFA) to import corn for them so they can avail of lower tariffs.
Local corn prices this week were mixed.
The NFA said white corn grains bought directly from the farmers were pegged at 6.48 pesos per kg from the previous 6.45 pesos while yellow corn fetched 6.46 pesos per kg from 6.41 pesos.
Traders, however, said they bought white grain corn at 7.40 pesos per kg and yellow corn at 7.20 pesos per kg.
In the retail market, the NFA said white corn was sold at 11.21 pesos per kg from 11.33 pesos while yellow corn was sold at 10.79 pesos per kg from 10.85 pesos.
Conversion US$=26.20
